rows.subtype: Approach: sort out runway with a cash and expense count [Thinking]
rows.description: After a layoff at a startup, the employee counts savings, essential monthly costs and expected severance to see how many months of runway exist. The number turns a vague fear into a bounded problem.

rows.subtype: Approach: structured job search with weekly targets [Action]
rows.description: The employee sets a weekly plan: update the CV, apply to ten roles, message five former colleagues and practice one mock interview. A routine gives a sense of progress even when replies are slow.

rows.subtype: Approach: take the first offer accepted out of panic [Pitfall]
rows.description: Fearing the gap, the employee accepts a role with lower pay and a poor fit without asking about terms. Within three months the person is looking again, showing how fear can override checking the match.

rows.subtype: Approach: revise the plan after two months without offers [Revision]
rows.description: With no offers after two months, the person reviews the applications, finds the CV lacks results-oriented lines, asks a mentor for feedback and widens the search to adjacent roles. Reviewing evidence prevents repeating a failing approach.

rows.subtype: Approach: ignoring the teasing at first [Thinking]
rows.description: A boy hopes that if he does not react the bully will get bored, and for some days it works a little, though it also shows the limits of ignoring when the teasing continues.

rows.subtype: Approach: rehearsing a calm firm reply [Thinking]
rows.description: In front of a mirror, a boy practises saying stop it in a steady voice and walking away, imagining how the bully will react so he is less shaken in the moment.

rows.subtype: Approach: hitting back in anger [Pitfall]
rows.description: A boy pushes the bully during recess and ends up in the principal's office too, learning that revenge can turn a victim into a person also in trouble.

rows.subtype: Approach: changing the plan when the first step fails [Revision]
rows.description: When ignoring the teasing does not stop it, the girl chooses to tell her parents, who meet the teacher, and the school separates the seating and watches the group.

rows.subtype: Approach: retracing steps [Action]
rows.description: A child looks for a lost shoe by going back through the day: the bedroom, the verandah, the gate where she played. Going in order narrows down where it could be.

rows.subtype: Approach: asking an adult [Action]
rows.description: A child says, "Mummy, I can't find my shoe," and mother asks, "Where did you last have it?" The adult's question gives the search a structure.

rows.subtype: Approach: magical thinking [Pitfall]
rows.description: A child insists that the shoe "ran away" and that it will come home if she waits at the door. Waiting replaces searching.

rows.subtype: Approach: copying a peer [Revision]
rows.description: A friend says, "Check the last place you played," and the child goes to the balcony where the shoe lies. The hint changes the search from random to reasoned.

rows.subtopic: Delivering bad news to a client
rows.subtype: Approach: preparing facts, cause and options first [Thinking]
rows.description: Before telling a hospital client that go-live will slip by three weeks, the account lead gathers the cause, the new date and two ways to reduce impact, so the message has substance.

rows.subtopic: Delivering bad news to a client
rows.subtype: Approach: mental rehearsal of likely reactions [Thinking]
rows.description: He imagines the client being angry, asking whom to blame, or asking for a discount. He drafts calm, honest replies for each so he is not pushed into rash promises.

rows.subtopic: Delivering bad news to a client
rows.subtype: Approach: delaying until a fix is found [Pitfall]
rows.description: Hoping to solve it quietly, the manager waits two weeks before telling the client. When the delay is finally revealed, trust suffers more than the delay itself would have caused.

rows.subtopic: Delivering bad news to a client
rows.subtype: Approach: reviewing the call and adjusting communication cadence [Revision]
rows.description: After the call the team notes the client wanted more frequent updates. They switch from weekly emails to short Monday and Thursday notes, and the relationship steadies.

rows.subtype: Approach: gathering specific examples before speaking [Thinking]
rows.description: A lead lists what actually happened: three late tasks and two untested changes over a month. He avoids labels like careless, so the discussion stays on observable work.

rows.subtype: Approach: root cause analysis with the junior [Thinking]
rows.description: In a private talk she asks what is making tasks hard. The junior explains he does not understand the codebase and fears asking, so the problem is support, not effort.

rows.subtype: Approach: doing the junior's work quietly [Pitfall]
rows.description: To meet deadlines the lead rewrites his code at night without telling him. He never learns what was wrong, and she burns out while his performance stays the same.

rows.subtype: Approach: adjusting the plan when the fit is wrong [Revision]
rows.description: After six weeks progress is patchy on backend but strong on testing. With the manager's agreement, the lead moves him to a quality role that suits his strengths.

rows.subtype: Approach: working backward from the loan end date [Thinking]
rows.description: A graduate with a Rs 6 lakh education loan takes the bank's repayment period and works backward to the monthly amount needed, then checks it against the expected salary. The goal date sets the size of each step.

rows.subtype: Approach: list loan terms and interest rate before deciding [Action]
rows.description: The borrower collects the sanction letter, notes the interest rate, moratorium end, EMI and any prepayment charges, and asks the bank to explain anything unclear. Knowing exact terms comes before choosing any strategy.

rows.subtype: Approach: ignore the letters until the first EMI is overdue [Pitfall]
rows.description: Anxious about the size of the loan, the graduate avoids opening bank messages during the moratorium. The first EMI is missed, a late fee is added and the credit record suffers. Avoidance turns a manageable task into a bigger problem.

rows.subtype: Approach: talk to the bank about restructuring before missing a payment [Revision]
rows.description: When a job start is delayed, the borrower meets the bank branch early, explains the situation and asks about options such as a longer tenure. Acting before default keeps choices open and shows good faith.
